rationale:
The candidate is a complete, executable grader whose public contract matches its implementation, whose five endpoints cover every eligible scientific result in the source, and whose 18 freshly executed controls (reference, empty, misplaced, 5 missing, recomputed, alternative, 4 wrong-value probes, file-deletion probe, 2 representation controls) all met their expected outcomes on the current candidate hash.

Source coverage: the source notebook has exactly five terminal scientific results — A (open-vs-closed backbone RMSD via rms.rmsd), B (backbone-fit trajectory RMSD with unweighted CORE/LID/NMP residual groups), C (CORE alpha-carbon RMSD), D (mass-weighted), E (residue-number-weighted). The earlier preparation plan excluded A and B from export only for serialization/recovery reasons (variable overwriting, unnamed expression), which are not valid scientific reasons to discard independent results; this task correctly restores both by re-running the identical source code path on the byte-identical copied inputs (materialize_a_b), and the public question, reference tables and checks cover all five endpoints. Nothing else in the source (plots, 'Time (ns)' column, shape prints) is an eligible scientific result. Plots and header metadata are legitimately excluded.

Contract/implementation match: the addendum's acceptance rule |v−r| ≤ 1e-5 + 1e-9·|r| (inclusive, reference denominator) matches TOL_ABS/TOL_REL and the code's `deviation > allowance` failure condition; headers, single data row for A, complete contiguous 0..F-1 frame series with reference-derived row count, finite/nonnegative/integer-frame rules, missing/nested-path-as-missing, and per-row one-to-one comparison are all implemented exactly as published. The dropped-frames loophole flagged in the probe concerns is in fact closed by code: load_trajectory_output requires frames == list(range(len(frames))) and check_trajectory_output compares the submission row count to the reference count. The grader emits all six declared checks exactly once for every submission kind, never crashes on malformed input, and contains no control-name detection or hardcoded values.

The previously open D-semantics risk (question defines mass-weighted group RMSDs while the notebook prose claims the group selections stay unweighted under weights='mass') is closed by controller-measured evidence, not by widened tolerance: both the recomputed control (MDAnalysis 2.11, weights='mass' without explicit weights_groupselections) and the alternative control (independent weighted-Kabsch solution with explicitly mass-weighted CORE/LID/NMP group RMSDs) passed every value cell against the same reference projection within the 1e-5 bound. Since unweighted vs mass-weighted backbone group RMSDs would deviate by orders of magnitude above 1e-5 at the mult-Å values in these tables, both passing establishes that the reference values are mass-weighted as the question states; the notebook prose is contradicted by its own recorded reference, and the question matches the reference.

Tolerance basis is defensible and honestly bounded: recorded frame-0 rounding is ≤ 5.2e-7 Å, 5-decimal rounding contributes ≤ 5e-6 Å (arithmetic, verified), the 9-decimal A control passes, and rejection is demonstrated (2e-5 Å perturbation fails with margin, plus wrong-method deviations 1e-3 to ~3.5 Å). The addendum explicitly discloses the bound's honest limits (sub-tolerance single-cell errors pass by construction; weighting schemes can agree ~1e-7 Å at frame 0) instead of claiming universal wrong-method detection. The np.float64(...) cell form is a representation-only rule, is disclosed publicly, is applied symmetrically (the reference B table itself carries such cells), and is validated by the reference control.

Repair-path verification: initial_probes differs from probes only in the repr-format-control rationale, whose correction is accurate — the frozen script writes plain '%.17g' in both branches of its dead conditional, so no np.float64(...) cell was produced by the mutation, and the corrected annotation attributes np.float64 acceptance to the reference control and the probe's own parse-back assertions. Mutation scripts, check_ids, kinds and intended outcomes are unchanged, and all 18 controls were re-executed on the revised candidate rather than inherited from the author's history.

Non-blocking observations are listed in issues; none affect which submissions pass.

source_coverage.rationale: Audited the original notebook, the preparation plan and the export code. The source computes exactly five terminal scientific results: the open-vs-closed pairwise backbone RMSD (rms.rmsd with center/superposition), the unweighted backbone-fit trajectory RMSD with CORE/LID/NMP residual group RMSDs (first rms.RMSD run), the CORE alpha-carbon-restricted trajectory RMSD (AtomGroup RMSD), the mass-weighted trajectory RMSD, and the residue-number-weighted trajectory RMSD. The preparation plan's exports captured only C, D and E and excluded A and B on purely serialization/recovery grounds (variable overwritten at completion; A never assigned to a variable). Those exclusion rationales are not valid scientific exclusions, but the constructed task correctly restores both excluded endpoints: the derive code copies the inputs byte-for-byte and materializes A and B by re-running the identical source code path (same selections, same RMSD class call, ref_frame=0), and the public question, check inventory and reference tables include A and B. All five endpoints are preserved in one task with no scientific scope change. The remaining source content (plots, 'Time (ns)' header metadata column, shape prints, narrative) is diagnostic/presentational and is legitimately not an output. The one consequential semantic question — the question's mass-weighted D group RMSDs versus the notebook prose claiming group selections stay unweighted under weights='mass' — is resolved by controller-measured evidence: both the recomputed MDAnalysis 2.11 control and the independent weighted-Kabsch alternative (with explicitly mass-weighted group RMSDs) passed every value cell against the same reference projection within 1e-5, which is only possible if the recorded reference values are mass-weighted as the question defines. No unsupported evidence claims or missing eligible branches remain.
